text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid said relief will be provided to the Karachi-based ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) to enable it to contest the February 3 general elections.

- A spokesman for caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid denied newspapers reports quoting him as saying that the IMF had disbursed the loan to Pakistan only after it was assured that ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's government would not be restored.
- Ten people were killed and 10 severely injured in a road accident in Rawalpindi.
- A team of Japan's Nomura Securities arrived in Pakistan to work out a deal with the government for the privatisation of state-run Pakistan Telecom Corporation Limited.
- Despite adverse circumstances, Pakistan's economy grew six percent as computed by the IMF in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June).
- Local polyester staple fibre prices have been reduced to 72 rupees per kg from 74 rupees because of a fall in international prices.
- The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry asked the government to give special incentives to the local engineering industry before opening up trade with India.
- Despite devaluation of the rupee by more than 17 percent against the dollar in 1996, textile exports grew only 6.76 percent in the last 11 months.
- About 10 percent of natural gas is wasted in pipeline leakages in Pakistan compared to one percent in other parts of the world.
- Traders urged the government to allow exports of red chillies as a surplus of around 20,000 tonnes is expected.

- Sita White, who says cricketer-turned-politician Imran Khan is the father of her daughter Tyrian, intends to visit Pakistan with her daughter during Khan's election campaign. Khan said the scandal was the brain-child of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif.
- The caretaker government is reluctant to scrap regulatory duty on imports in spite of pressure from within the country and international financial institutions.
- India has announced that it will buy four new submarines to enhance its navy's offensive capabilities.

- The Pakistan People's Party led by ousted prime minister Bneazir Bhutto has decided to participate in the February 3 elections and to kick off its campaign from the village of President Farooq Leghari, who dimissed Bhutto on November 5.
